title: Establish accessible delta palettes and modular typographic scale for micro-controls
creator: Ava Mitchell
description:
Problem: Our current token set prioritizes broad surface coverage but causes friction in high-density micro-controls (small buttons, compact dropdowns, dense table rows). Small UI elements are sensitive to subtle color shifts, tight radius values, and shallow shadows; inconsistent deltas lead to perceptual inconsistency and accessibility regressions in low-contrast and scaled-font scenarios.

Proposal: Introduce a small, focused token subset that we call 'delta palettes' — explicit contrast delta steps that sit on top of our semantic palette and are tuned for micro-controls. Pair this with a modular typographic micro-scale (3-step micro-scale anchored to base type) and a compact radius family with gesture-aware thresholds. Also define a set of shallow, Lambert-inspired shadow presets for layered data rows and micro action bars to improve perceived depth without reducing legibility.

Goals:
- Ensure AA+ contrast for primary and secondary micro-controls at UI text sizes down to 11px across light/dark modes.
- Provide a modular micro-type scale that maps to tokens (micro-XS, micro-S, micro-M) and aligns with spacing/radius deltas.
- Standardize radius tokens for touch vs. pointer targets (gesture-aware thresholds).
- Introduce 3 low-cost shadow presets that render well on mid-range GPUs and in VPC/private deployments (avoids heavy blur kernels).

Scope: Buttons (compact variants), table rows (dense mode), chart micro-controls (legends, small toggles), and form micro-controls (inline selects, tag chips). Not covering full-component rework or large-scale theme rewrites in this ticket; that will be in follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria:
- Define delta-palette tokens: delta-01, delta-02, delta-03 with precise WCAG contrast ratios measured against both base neutral and accent anchors (provide HEXs).
- Publish micro type tokens: micro-xs, micro-s, micro-m with font-size, line-height, and letter-spacing.
- Publish radius tokens: r-gesture, r-pointer, r-min with clear usage guidance and accessibility rationale.
- Publish shadow presets: shadow-micro-1, shadow-micro-2, shadow-micro-3 with GPU-cost notes and fallbacks.
- Dev-ready token JSON and changelog in Design Tokens repo.
- Confluence spec page with examples, migration notes, and acceptance screenshots for light/dark modes.
- Designer + Frontend sign-off and at least one integration PR that updates compact Button and Dense Table Row stories in Storybook.
- Automated visual diff baseline created and checked into QA pipeline.
engineering_notes:
- Token JSON must follow existing token schema and include metadata fields: description, category, intended_use.
- Shadow presets should avoid 40px gaussian blurs; prefer stacked 2-layer blurs with alpha ramp to reduce kernel size.
- Typographic tokens must support responsive rem-based usage for Redwood Console and Portable CSS variables for Private deployments.
- Provide a small performance test measuring paint cost of shadows on a 3rd-gen mid-range GPU; add results into PR description.
- Add feature flag for dense-mode token rollout to avoid immediate global changes.
- Link PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/design-tokens/pull/721
migration_plan: 1) Ship token JSON behind a 'dense-micro-tokens' feature flag. 2) Update compact Button and Dense Table components to read new tokens in Storybook. 3) Run visual diffs and manual accessibility checks. 4) Gradual rollout to Console with Canary (5% -> 25% -> 100%). 5) Add notes to customer-facing changelog and migration guide for Dedicated/Private customers. 6) After 30 days of telemetry, deprecate legacy compact tokens and provide codemods for internal repos.
risks_and_tradeoffs:
- Risk: Slightly increased cognitive surface for designers due to extra micro tokens; mitigate with clear docs and examples.
- Tradeoff: Shadows tuned for performance may not match 'designer-perfect' depth; acceptance criteria prioritize legibility and cost.
- Risk: Some legacy product screens rely on previous micro contrast values; will need follow-up audits.
- Mitigation: Provide a migration checklist and two-week support window after rollout.
